chief_complaint: electric pain down lateral lower leg, normal reflexes
hpi_details: 61-year-old male complains of sharp, electric-like pain shooting down the back and outside of his left leg, extending to the top of his foot and big toe. Pain worsens with walking and standing. Reflexes are completely normal.
ideas: He thinks he severely tore a muscle or pinched a nerve deep in his hip while working around the house.
concerns: He is worried that he will need spinal surgery or become unable to stay on his feet long enough to keep his job.
expectations: He hopes to get a prescription for strong pain medicine and a referral to physical therapy so he can walk normally again.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of L5 radiculopathy is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Sciatica L5 root: NSAIDs when appropriate, physical therapy, and selective transforaminal epidural injection, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.

dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: saddle anesthesia, bladder dysfunction, or progressive foot drop, which require emergency imaging rather than routine conservative management.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: electric pain down lateral lower leg, normal reflexes

61-year-old male complains of sharp, electric-like pain shooting down the back and outside of his left leg, extending to the top of his foot and big toe. Pain worsens with walking and standing. Reflexes are completely normal.
reference_soap.objective: Positive straight leg raise on the left at 45 degrees. Weakness in left extensor hallucis longus (great toe extension, 4/5). Normal patellar (L4) and Achilles (S1) reflexes. Diminished sensation over the dorsal first web space.
reference_soap.assessment: L5 Radiculopathy, likely due to L4-L5 disc herniation or foraminal stenosis.
reference_soap.plan: Use a short course of NSAIDs if appropriate and refer to physical therapy. Obtain lumbar MRI promptly for progressive motor weakness or after persistent symptoms despite conservative management.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Sciatica L5 root
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Sciatica L5 root
Implement evidence-based management plan: NSAIDs when appropriate, physical therapy, and selective transforaminal epidural injection

teaching.one_liner: Irritation of the L5 nerve root causing electric shooting pain down the outer lower leg, often with normal reflexes.
red_flags: Bilateral leg symptoms with saddle anesthesia and bowel/bladder dysfunction — concerning for cauda equina syndrome
Progressive motor weakness or foot drop
Fever or unexplained weight loss — raising suspicion for infection or malignancy

must_ask.say: Does the pain shoot down the outside of your lower leg?
What makes it worse — standing, walking?
How is this affecting your daily activities?

history.answer: Doctor, I have this sharp, electric pain shooting down the outside of my left leg.
It starts around my lower back and hip and shoots down the back and outside of my left leg, all the way to the top of my foot and big toe.
It started about two weeks ago, and I do not remember lifting anything heavy or falling down.
It feels like a sharp electric jolt or shooting lightning, and at its worst it gets up to a 6 or 7 out of 10.
The pain gets much worse when I walk or stand for a while, and it eases up when I lie down with my knees bent.
Whenever I cough hard, sneeze, or strain, I feel a sudden electric jolt shoot down my leg.
It does not keep me awake at night, and lying down in bed usually helps calm the pain down.
I do not have morning stiffness lasting half an hour; it just feels a bit stiff for a minute until I get moving.
The top of my left foot feels numb and tingly, and lifting my left big toe feels slightly weak compared to my right.
No, I have no numbness around my groin or buttocks, and my bladder and bowel control are completely normal.
Walking definitely brings on the pain, but bending forward does not relieve it; only sitting or lying down helps.
No, I have had no fever, chills, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss.
No, I have never had any cancer or tumors.
No recent infections, no spinal injections or procedures, and I do not have diabetes or use needle drugs.
I do not have osteoporosis, and I have never taken steroid pills or had any falls.
No abdominal pain, no pulsing feelings in my belly, and no burning or blood when I urinate.
No eye redness, heel pain, ongoing diarrhea, or skin conditions like psoriasis.
I tried taking over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen a few times, but they only helped slightly.
It makes walking for long periods and doing household chores difficult because I have to sit down frequently.
I thought I must have torn a tendon or pinched something deep in my hip from heavy yard work.
I'm worried I might need invasive surgery or that I won't be able to stay on my feet to do my job.
I'm hoping to walk out with some stronger pain medicine and maybe a referral for physical therapy so I can move without pain.
My health has always been good, with no high blood pressure, diabetes, or other chronic conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications, regular over-the-counter pills, or herbal supplements.
No, I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink socially, maybe a beer or two on occasion.
I work an office job at a desk, and I live with my wife.
No one in my family has serious spine disorders or nerve conditions.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 125/80 mmHg, pulse 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Normal lumbar spinal curvature without midline bony tenderness; straight leg raise is positive on the left at 45 degrees reproducing radiating leg pain.
Weakness in left extensor hallucis longus with great toe extension graded 4/5, while strength in all other bilateral lower extremity muscle groups is 5/5.
Diminished pinprick and light touch sensation over the left dorsal first web space and lateral lower leg, with sensation otherwise intact bilaterally.
Patellar and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally, with down-going plantar responses.
Antalgic gait favouring the left lower extremity, but able to perform heel and toe walking without foot drop.
Normal resting anal sphincter tone and intact voluntary contraction, with preserved perianal sensation.
Abdomen is soft and non-tender without palpable mass or abnormal aortic pulsation.
